record.paper_title: QCD, from its inception to its stubbornly unsolved problems
record.original_question: Can QCD provide a quantitatively satisfactory first-principles account of hadronization and of the underlying event, rather than relying on phenomenological tuning, machine-learning-assisted tuning, string models, or cluster models, and can it justify factorization in this full realistic setting rather than treating factorization as an ansatz?

evidence.quote: Its green parts (hadronization and the “underlying” event) are not understood at the quite satisfactory level of its hard scattering and QCD shower parts.
They are treated by “phenomenological” methods requiring a back-and-forth zitterbewegung between predictions and observations, to tune parameters and/or coach a machine learning program.
The hadronization issue is tackled by non-quantum-mechanical methods, such as stretching frangible strings or gathering colorless clusters.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Quantum Chromodynamics (QCD) is the non-abelian gauge theory with gauge group SU(3) describing the strong interaction of quarks and gluons, with Lagrangian
  L = -(1/4) G^a_{μν} G^{a μν} + Σ_f \bar{ψ}_f (i γ^μ D_μ - m_f) ψ_f,
where D_μ = ∂_μ - i g_s t^a A^a_μ and G^a_{μν} is the non-abelian field strength. In high-energy hadronic collisions, observable cross sections receive contributions from (i) a perturbatively calculable hard partonic scattering, (ii) a perturbative parton shower describing collinear/soft radiation, (iii) hadronization, the non-perturbative transition from colored partons to color-singlet hadrons, and (iv) the underlying event, the additional soft activity associated with spectator partons of the colliding hadrons. In current practice, components (iii) and (iv) are modeled by phenomenological prescriptions such as the Lund string model or cluster hadronization model, with parameters fixed by tuning to data (possibly using machine learning), and the validity of factorization theorems—the statement that the cross section can be written as a convolution of process-independent non-perturbative functions (parton distributions, fragmentation functions) with perturbatively computable hard kernels—is in this full realistic setting effectively assumed as an ansatz beyond the regimes where it has been rigorously proved.

Problem. Provide a first-principles derivation, directly from the QCD Lagrangian above, that:
(a) gives a quantitatively predictive description of hadronization, i.e. computes from QCD alone (without recourse to tuned phenomenological string or cluster models) the probability distributions for a system of colored partons to evolve into a definite final state of hadrons, in agreement with experimental data;
(b) gives a first-principles description of the underlying event in hadron–hadron collisions; and
(c) establishes factorization of inclusive and semi-inclusive hadronic cross sections in this realistic full setting, including the contributions of (a) and (b), as a theorem derived from QCD rather than as an assumed ansatz.
artifact.status_search_result: Hadronization, the underlying event, and a fully general proof of factorization remain widely acknowledged open problems in QCD. Factorization theorems have been rigorously proved only for restricted classes of processes (e.g., inclusive DIS, Drell–Yan, certain semi-inclusive observables), while hadronization is still treated via phenomenological string/cluster models tuned to data, including ML-assisted tuning in modern Monte Carlo event generators. No first-principles QCD derivation of hadronization or the underlying event exists as of recent reviews.

status_evidence.title: QCD, from its inception to its stubbornly unsolved problems
status_evidence.snippet: Hadronization and the underlying event are not understood at the satisfactory level of hard scattering; treated by phenomenological methods.
status_evidence.claim: Hadronization and the underlying event remain unsolved from first principles in QCD.

status_evidence.title: Collins, Foundations of Perturbative QCD
status_evidence.snippet: Factorization theorems are proved for specific inclusive processes; general factorization in hadron-hadron collisions with full final-state effects is not established.
status_evidence.claim: Factorization is rigorously proved only in restricted settings; the general case remains an ansatz.
